heroHeadline: Resistance Strikes NW Regional Command HQ in Monywa — 8 Junta Killed; KIA Shifts to Defensive as SAC Pours 300-Vehicle Convoy into Kachin — Day 1,938
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,938 of Myanmar's civil war (May 24, 2026), resistance forces struck one of the SAC's most significant command targets since the coup: the Northwest Regional Military Command headquarters in Monywa, Sagaing Region, killing 8 junta personnel and injuring 20+ in a May 23 rocket attack confirmed by the NUG's Deputy Minister of Home Affairs. The Monywa NW Command oversees SAC operations across the entire Sagaing and Mandalay theaters — the strike exposes the command overextension created by the junta's simultaneous multi-front offensive surge. That surge also prompted a strategic response from the Kachin Independence Army, which announced a temporary defensive posture on May 22 after the SAC dispatched a 300-vehicle armored convoy with mobile howitzers from Mandalay to the Northern Military Command in Myitkyina — the largest Kachin reinforcement in years. KIA retains all captured positions: Myitkyina remains encircled, IB-58 in Waingmaw is besieged at 100 meters, and the Hpakant jade-mining corridor is KIA-controlled. Meanwhile, the Arakan Army continues advancing on Kyaukphyu — China's $7.3-billion CMEC deep-sea port — with SAC jets and warships maintaining bombardment of Sanae Township. The UN warns that 16.2 million people — one-third of Myanmar's population — now require humanitarian aid, with 12 million facing acute hunger in 2026 and displacement projected to reach 4 million as the junta's ongoing offensive surge drives new mass displacements across Rakhine, Chin, Tanintharyi, and Sagaing.
